scores.evidence: The s4-sort flowchart TD has short three-line Japanese labels that stay readable at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-18.png). The two code blocks s3-code and p-model-code keep their line numbers when long lines wrap (pages/mobile-jp-13.png, pages/mobile-jp-29.png), and nothing is cut off or overlaps on any screen.

Every section starts with a lead and a definitions card, and a check follows within one or two screens. The practice section is long, though: p-steps (8 steps) is followed by p-prompt-write, p-prompt-green and p-prompt-review back to back, which fills about six mobile screens without a break (pages/mobile-jp-23.png to pages/mobile-jp-28.png). Only mobile screen 4 counts as text-only, and it still holds a definitions card and a bold-keyed list.

All visible text is Japanese, with English terms in parentheses on first use. Diagram labels are in Japanese, and s4-sort has an alt text. Contrast is good on the callouts, chips and dark code blocks. The controls are not hidden under the top bar or the mobile bottom bar. No personal data appears on any screen.

niceToHave: Mobile code wrap: in p-model-code line 5 the lone `{` wraps onto its own row ("() =>" / "{"), and in s3-code line 5 `=> {` wraps (pages/mobile-jp-29.png, pages/mobile-jp-13.png). It is still readable, but shorter test names such as test('4の倍数はうるう年', …) would keep each line on one row at 390 px.

s3-prompt-write, s3-prompt-green, s2-goal-prompt and the practice prompts show raw backticks around identifiers. On mobile this causes awkward breaks such as "空文字" / "は `false`。" (pages/mobile-jp-12.png). Dropping the backticks in the prompt text (the identifiers are clear without them) would read more cleanly, and the copied prompt would not change in meaning.

Practice section rhythm: think about moving each of p-prompt-write, p-prompt-green and p-prompt-review next to the step that uses it (or adding a short markdown line between them), so the three prompt cards do not stack after the 8-step list (pages/mobile-jp-25.png to pages/mobile-jp-28.png).

Desktop: the s4-sort diagram is taller than one 900 px screen (pages/desktop-jp-11.png to pages/desktop-jp-12.png), so the whole flow cannot be seen at once. The expand button helps; slightly shorter node labels would make the figure less tall.
reader: the flashcard hint says 'クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる' on the 390 px mobile view, where tap is the input (pages/mobile-jp-36.png).
reader: steps that only have a `hint` (p-green, p-review) are still labelled 'うまくいかないときは' (pages/mobile-jp-24.png, pages/desktop-jp-16.png).
reader: the desktop '用語・このレッスン' panel lists 10 of the 15 glossary terms (/goal, エッジケース, 過剰設計, Explanatory and Learning are missing) (pages/desktop-jp-01.png).
reader: the end banner says this is the course's last lesson because drafts are not in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-38.png, pages/desktop-jp-25.png). This is a known preview state.
reader: the mobile full-length PNG stops at 16000 px, and 14 failed /api/ requests were ignored as environment noise. Both are known preview states.
summary: The metrics show no hard failures (no horizontal overflow, console, mermaid, unknown-block or image errors), and no personal data appears on any screen. Desktop JP has a median of 39 characters per line, inside the 30–40 target. The s4-sort flowchart and both code blocks stay readable at 390 px. The biggest strength is the steady rhythm of lead, definitions card, prompt or code, then inline check. The most useful improvement is in the practice section: break up the three prompt cards that follow the 8-step list, and shorten the test names in p-model-code so line 5 does not wrap on mobile.
